_format.name: Place name
_format.category: cafe | food | pub | viewpoint | attraction | museum | castle | park | shop | walk
_format.description: One or two characterful sentences: why it's worth a stop

places.name: Calton Hill
places.description: Five minutes' climb from the bus station for the best skyline in Edinburgh: castle, Arthur's Seat and the Forth in one sweep.

places.name: Edinburgh Castle
places.description: Perched on an extinct volcano above Princes Street. Time it for the One O'Clock Gun.

places.name: Scottish National Gallery
places.description: Free, central and right by Princes Street. Raeburn's skating minister is the one everyone looks for.

places.name: Arthur's Seat
places.description: A proper hill in the middle of the city. Allow an hour up and down if your group has time to kill.

places.name: Dean Village
places.description: A storybook mill village tucked below the West End. Follow the Water of Leith for a quiet stroll.

places.name: The Oxford Bar
places.description: A tiny, no-frills New Town pub, famous as Inspector Rebus's local.

places.name: Edinburgh Zoo
places.description: Right at the bus stop. Catch the penguins' 'Wee Waddle' walk on Thursday to Sunday afternoons.

places.name: Glasgow Necropolis
places.description: A Victorian city of the dead on a hill behind the cathedral. Atmospheric, free, with big views over Glasgow.

places.name: Gallery of Modern Art
places.description: Free art in a grand old building, guarded by the Duke of Wellington statue and his traffic-cone hat.

places.name: Mackintosh at the Willow
places.description: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's restored 1903 tearooms on Sauchiehall Street. Afternoon tea with a design history lesson.

places.name: Glasgow Green
places.description: Glasgow's oldest park, with the huge terracotta Doulton Fountain and the Venetian-style Templeton carpet factory.

places.name: The Barras
places.description: Glasgow's legendary weekend market: vintage finds, oddities and Barrowland Ballroom's neon sign.

places.name: V&A Dundee
places.description: Kengo Kuma's cliff-like building on the Tay. Free Scottish Design Galleries and a great café.

places.name: RRS Discovery
places.description: Scott's Antarctic expedition ship, built in Dundee and moored next to the V&A.

places.name: Jute Café Bar at DCA
places.description: The arts centre's buzzy café bar. Good food, and a cinema if you're early.

places.name: Dundee Law
places.description: An old volcano in the middle of the city. 360° views over the Tay bridges.

places.name: Dundee Botanic Garden
places.description: The university's peaceful garden by the river, with glasshouses for a rainy day.

places.name: Perth Museum
places.description: Home of the Stone of Destiny since 2024, in the grand old City Hall. Free, but book a time slot to see the Stone.

places.name: North Inch
places.description: A huge riverside green on the Tay. Perfect for a picnic while you wait for friends.

places.name: Perth Art Gallery
places.description: Free, and home to the world's largest collection of Scottish Colourist J.D. Fergusson's bold paintings.

places.name: Pitlochry Dam & Fish Ladder
places.description: Watch salmon leap up the fish ladder (in season), then walk across the dam over Loch Faskally.

places.name: Blair Athol Distillery
places.description: A whisky distillery that's been going since 1798, a short walk from the bus.

places.name: Pitlochry Festival Theatre
places.description: Over the footbridge by the river, with a café and Explorers Garden attached.

places.name: Stirling Castle
places.description: One of Scotland's grandest castles. The Great Hall and Stirling Heads are the highlights.

places.name: The King's Knot
places.description: A mysterious grassy geometric garden below the castle. Some say it's where Arthur's Round Table stood.

places.name: McCaig's Tower
places.description: Oban's own Colosseum on the hill. Free, and the best view of the bay and the islands.

places.name: Oban Distillery
places.description: One of Scotland's smallest distilleries, right on the main street.

places.name: Oban Seafood Hut
places.description: The famous little green shack by the ferry pier. Fresh langoustines and scallops eaten standing up.

places.name: Inverness Castle
places.description: The red sandstone castle above the River Ness reopened in 2026 as the Inverness Castle Experience. Panoramic views, gardens and a café.

places.name: Ness Islands
places.description: Wooded islands in the river, linked by Victorian footbridges. A 20-minute riverside stroll from the centre.

places.name: Leakey's Bookshop
places.description: One of Scotland's largest second-hand bookshops, in an old church with a wood-burning stove.

places.name: Footdee (Fittie)
places.description: A quirky fishermen's village at the harbour mouth, with painted sheds. Look out for dolphins.

places.name: Aberdeen Art Gallery
places.description: A beautifully refurbished gallery with a rooftop view over the Granite City.

places.name: King's College, Old Aberdeen
places.description: A cobbled medieval university quarter with a crown-topped chapel from 1500.

places.name: Bracklinn Falls
places.description: A woodland walk from Callander to a gorge and a dramatic waterfall bridge.

places.name: The Real Food Café
places.description: The legendary West Highland Way pit stop in Tyndrum. Fish and chips worth changing buses for.
